children: Quantum computing stocks moved higher Tuesday after three companies secured $100 million each in U.S. government funding, while IonQ lifted its 2026 revenue forecast.

The funding agreements involve D-Wave, Rigetti and Quantinuum, with each receiving $100 million from the U.S. Department of Commerce through the CHIPS and Science Act. The government will receive minority equity positions under the arrangements.
The money is intended for research and development rather than immediate sales, giving recipients additional resources to address technical challenges as they develop larger quantum systems.

IonQ provided a separate catalyst, raising its 2026 revenue outlook to $450 million to $460 million from $280 million to $290 million previously. The company also introduced its Superion 256 platform and said customer deliveries are planned for 2027.
D-Wave Quantum (QBTS) gained 6%, while Rigetti Computing (RGTI) rose 4%. Quantum Computing (QUBT) added 2.6%, and IonQ (IONQ) climbed 2% even as the broader market traded lower.
Investors may now focus on whether the funding and higher forecasts translate into commercial progress and improved financial performance.

title: D-Wave, Rigetti and IonQ Stocks Rally on $100 Million Quantum Boost
